isolation: Each scenario drove its own independent OAuth2/PKCE sign-in against Thunder SSO (a fresh browser session per caller: acc-abdd7afecb14 for Sam, acc-jordan-1791044408 for Jordan, both against the test-caller login published on the roles-gate ticket) and called the deployed GET /greeting endpoint directly. The endpoint is stateless and read-only (no container to own), so isolation came from using fresh, independent sign-ins per scenario rather than from a resettable resource; no shared state was mutated or depended upon between scenarios.

scenarios.rule: Only a signed-in caller may request the greeting
scenarios.scenario: A signed-in caller receives the greeting

steps.text: Sam has signed in via Thunder SSO
steps.command: agent-browser PKCE authorize against development-idp.openchoreo.localhost:8080/oauth2/authorize (session acc-abdd7afecb14), signed in as test-caller, then fetch POST /oauth2/token from the page context to exchange the code
grep -q '^HTTP/1.1 200' /tmp/sam_authed_headers.txt && python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(open('/tmp/sam_authed_body.json')); sys.exit(0 if d.get('message') else 1)"

scenarios.rule: Only a signed-in caller may request the greeting

steps.command: no token obtained — no sign-in performed
